_readme: THE LANE CONTRACT (DRE-2726). One file, read by everything.
Per lane: the entrance condition, the exit condition, the permitted writers,
and the evidence that justifies occupancy. The guard (scripts/lane_scope.py)
reads its flow from here instead of carrying a copy; the sweep
(scripts/reconcile.py) reads its stall windows from here; the documentation
(docs/lane-contract.md) is RENDERED from here; and the integration harness
asserts the live board against it on every trunk commit.
Every clause carries `enforced_from`: the wave phase at which the harness may
assert it. The harness asserts only clauses whose phase has shipped, and FAILS
when a clause's phase has passed with nothing implementing it. That is what
makes this a schedule that checks itself rather than a description.
JSON, not YAML: scripts/linear_ops.py imports the reader on every product
repo's agent job, where there is no pip install and PyYAML is not guaranteed.
Regenerate the document after any edit:
python3 scripts/lane_contract.py render
Check the live board against it:
python3 scripts/lane_contract.py check --live
Wave 1.5's phases, and how far the wave has actually shipped. `current` is
advanced by the operator prove-cards (DRE-2760..DRE-2768) — and advancing it
is the whole act: every clause at or below it must have an implementation or
the harness fails.

titles.0: the checks that must exist before anything moves
titles.1: Linear set up and the Intake lane visible
titles.2: the lane contract asserted by the harness
titles.3: the gates proven against every card type
titles.4: the agents changed before they touch a card
titles.5: cards flow through the new front door
titles.6: the old structure archived, and the wave closed

why: The transition a card makes leaving the planning segment — where the second
critic writes its verdict. Layer 1 of the guard polices the lanes downstream
of it and nothing upstream, because upstream no verdict can exist yet.
Named after the transition, never after a description of the lanes on one
side of it: a description drifts and takes the guard's scope with it.

_readme: Retired board names, accepted on INPUT so a board mid-rename still resolves
to the right lane. An alias is not a lane and is never written out by the
contract; scripts/linear_ops.py inverts this map for the one write path that
still needs the old name. Delete an entry once no board carries it — this is
the ONE place the retired name survives, and both directions read it here.
Each entry carries the shim marker DRE-2722's sweep looks for, so the
exemption is a declared intent on the line itself and not a path allow-list.
The console's own state vocabulary, which must not diverge from the board.
It lives in another repository, so the harness locates the module by name in
that repo's tree and reads the named symbol. When it cannot reach it, the
clause reports UNEVALUATED — never a pass — and becomes a hard failure from
the phase named on the rule.
Every actor permitted to move a card, and where it lives. A lane names
writers by key; the harness checks the key resolves here and that a writer
with a path still exists in this checkout — a lane whose writer was deleted
is a lane nothing can legally move a card out of.
It is also the ACTOR GLOSSARY the act registry binds to (DRE-2825):
`pipeline_act.problems()` refuses an act whose `next_actor` is not a key
here, so that an act cannot hand work to somebody nothing knows about. An
entry may therefore name an actor no lane lists — `release-train.yml` is
one, added by DRE-3521 for the six release acts. Being in this glossary is
not permission to move a card: permission is a lane naming the key in its
own `writers` clause, which is what `ready_lane_writers.py` reads.

relay.what: the dispatch Lambda — creates a card's first lane from an inbound event
relay.note: lives in agent-bureau (cloud/relay); no path to check from here

operator.what: a human, working in Linear or running a script by hand

plan.yml.what: the planner — writes an epic's children and moves the epic for approval

agent-task.yml.what: the build run — takes a card from Todo and reports where it landed

agent-fix.yml.what: the fix run — REQUEST_CHANGES or a merge conflict

qa-review.yml.what: the adversarial critic — writes the verdict the gate reads

merge-gate.yml.what: the gate — merges on CI green plus a bound APPROVE

linear-sync.yml.what: the merge seam — closes the card off GitHub's merge event

reconcile.py.what: the ~15-minute sweep — promotion, staleness nudges, unsticking

linear_ops.py.what: the guarded write layer every other writer goes through

mid_epic.py.what: mid-epic discovery — files a sibling into an approved epic

dead_run.py.what: the dead-run cap — parks a card that keeps dying

groomer.py.what: the groomer — moves ONE approved batch out of Intake, in order

critic_score.py.what: the critic's audit — moves a card the critic could not classify, with the reason on it

backlog_cutover.py.what: the retroactive pass — moves the legacy Backlog into Intake, promoter-reach cards first and then newest-first, with no exemption list

release-train.yml.what: the release train — runs a surface's release script and verifies the tag it cut; it moves no card, and is here as the actor the six release acts name (DRE-3521)

guard.what: the lane guard — returns a card whose occupancy is unjustified
guard.note: DRE-2725, built in agent-bureau; reads its scope from lane_scope.py

rules.text: No state exists in Linear that the contract does not name.
rules.why: A leftover design-review state sat on the board with one card ever and zero code references, and nobody noticed for four months (DRE-2726 retired it; DRE-2818 deleted the last entry naming it).

rules.text: No lane is named that does not exist in Linear.
rules.why: The other half of the same pair: a contract that names a lane the board dropped is a contract nothing can satisfy.

rules.text: A retiring lane holds no cards.
rules.why: A lane the pipeline no longer writes to is a lane nothing will move a card out of. An occupied one is a stranded card.
rules.pending: Phase 3 is when the wave asserts it. Nothing is retiring today (DRE-2818 deleted the last two entries once Linear archived their states), so the clause is vacuously satisfied and skipped; it earns its keep on the NEXT retirement, where the sweep's drain (reconcile.drain_retiring_lanes) empties the lane and this is what proves the drain finished

rules.text: A retiring entry whose Linear state is already gone is deleted from this file.
rules.why: A retirement that never finishes is drift too. Once the board catches up, the entry is the last copy of a lane that no longer exists.

rules.text: Every lane the pipeline knows appears in the console's state lists, and the console names no state the contract does not carry.
rules.why: The console's vocabulary carried Proposed and HOLD, neither of which is a Linear state, and it renders an Intake column that can never fill.

rules.text: The pipeline's own scripts and workflows name no state the contract does not carry.
rules.why: A workflow that advances a card into an archived state fails its Linear call at 2am, on a card nobody is watching.

rules.text: Every transition observed was made by a writer the destination lane permits.
rules.why: A lane's writer list is only a contract if something reads the transition log against it.
rules.pending: needs the transition history the Phase-5 front door records

rules.text: Every transition observed carried the evidence the destination lane requires.
rules.why: The evidence clause is the one that makes occupancy justifiable rather than assumed.
rules.pending: the routing verdict exists and is readable (DRE-2724); still needed is the plan artifact gate (DRE-2720) and a writer that stamps every card at planning exit (DRE-2721)

entrance.text: Every writer that creates work writes here first — the relay, the planner, a mid-epic discovery, a human. There is no other valid first lane.
entrance.pending: DRE-2680 points every writer at Intake

exit.text: A classification exists: one-off, epic, or wave. There are exactly TWO ways out, and both are an approval the CEO gives. For a card nobody filed under an epic the way out is the groomer — it proposes a batch, the CEO approves it in Green Light, and the approved batch drains to Planning (groomer.py drain). For a card whose PARENT EPIC is being planned the way out is adoption (DRE-4668, on the CEO's signed answer of 2026-09-23): the planning exit writes the child's routing verdict and moves it to Backlog, where it waits — the epic's own green light is the approval for the cards filed under it, and nothing builds until the CEO moves that epic to In Progress. A child the verdict sends back to Planning is not adopted and stays here. AGE IS NOT AN EXIT: no card is moved out of this lane for being old, this lane carries no stall window, and there is no window of any length in its place (DRE-4141, on the CEO's signed answer of 2026-09-17). The sweep reports how many cards are waiting and how old the oldest is, and moves none of them.

writers.text: Anything that creates a card, and the retroactive pass that moves the legacy Backlog in. ONE of them also moves a card onward, and only with an approval behind it: plan.yml adopts a planned epic's own children into Backlog (DRE-4668). The groomer's drain — the other way out — writes Planning rather than this lane, so it is named as a writer there.

evidence.text: The card exists and carries no classification yet.

lanes.name: Planning
lanes.stale_why: what a Planning card owes is a classification, and producing one is a planner run — plan.yml's job alone is capped at 45 minutes, two planner passes and two critic rounds (DRE-2736, DRE-2721)

entrance.text: The card has been classified as needing a plan.

exit.text: The card leaves by the route its shape declares (DRE-2844): a one-off the check can route goes straight to the build queue, carrying the routing verdict its own card decided and owing no plan artifact and no green light — one whose card names no exit condition to route on takes the escalation exit below instead (DRE-3038). A one-off is READ BEFORE IT MOVES (DRE-3041): the same pre-approval critic an epic gets, one bounded call between the shape stamp and the move, asking whether this is one pull request of work an agent can build unattended with nothing in it that is a decision. A pass moves the card; anything else — including a critic that could not run — takes the escalation exit below rather than the build queue, because nothing reads a one-off after this point. An epic leaves for the CEO on a plan artifact, and for an epic it is still no artifact, no exit; a wave leaves to be decomposed into epics before anything is approved. A card carrying no shape is CLASSIFIED by the run before it routes (DRE-3029) — one bounded read of the card against the three shapes, stamped with who made the call and on which model — so nothing sits here owing a stamp a person has to write by hand. There is a fourth exit and it is the only one that is not a plan: the run ESCALATES, with a reason stated in business terms, and the card parks in Green Light (DRE-2848) — the classifier takes it for a card it cannot place, and the planner for an epic whose reasoning is itself the deliverable. Hand-planning is that escalation and nothing else — no label, flag or lane skips this lane, and the one sanctioned bypass past the Todo gate, `break-glass`, returns the card here for the classification it went round. The SWEEP takes that same fourth exit for a card nothing has happened to in the lane's stall window (DRE-4124): a card nobody can move belongs in the queue of the person who can, so it is escalated with its reason rather than labelled `needs-human` and left sitting here — which is what froze thirteen cards, the oldest for thirty-five days.
exit.pending: DRE-2720 writes the epic's artifact, DRE-2844 branches the exit on the shape and DRE-2848 adds the escalation exit; the gate that refuses an epic's exit without an artifact is Phase 5

writers.text: The planner, the sweep that re-triggers it, a build run handing back a card that turned out to be an epic, the groomer draining a batch the CEO approved, the critic's audit moving a card it could not classify, the guarded write layer every automated card-minting seam goes through — the Todo gate returning a card it cannot repair, the one-off producer, and the medic/watch seams that file a fresh card (DRE-2858) — and a human.

evidence.text: The plan artifact on the card: business case, KPIs as data, risk, outcome.

entrance.text: A plan is waiting on the CEO, an agent has escalated a question only the CEO can answer, the planner has escalated a card whose reasoning is itself the deliverable and stated why (DRE-2848), the post-approval critic sent an approved plan back with a stated reason (DRE-2721), a card has aged out of Intake and the sweep moved it here (DRE-2687), or a card has stood still in Planning past that lane's window and the sweep moved it here (DRE-4124 — the same remedy as the Intake age-out, one lane later: it used to be labelled for a human and left in Planning, where every other mechanism skips a held card and nobody was ever asked).
entrance.pending: needs the transition history the Phase-5 front door records — the four entrances exist, nothing yet reads a card's arrival against them

exit.text: The CEO answers: an approved plan activates — and its children promote only once the post-approval critic has read it (DRE-2721) — an answered escalation returns to Todo, a rejected one goes to Backlog.
exit.pending: needs the transition history the Phase-5 front door records

writers.text: The planner, the two agent runs that escalate, the sweep that moves a card out of Intake once it has aged past the window, and a human.

evidence.text: A plan artifact, an escalation comment written in business terms — never code, never a diff — or a `plan-critic:` marker recording the round that sent the plan back (DRE-2721).
evidence.pending: needs routing verdicts (DRE-2724) writing on every card before arrival can be judged against the evidence

entrance.text: It carries a routing verdict — one of the five in config/routing-verdicts.json, machine-readable on the card.
entrance.pending: the vocabulary exists (DRE-2724); what is still missing is a writer that puts a verdict on EVERY card at planning exit — DRE-2721's second critic

exit.text: The verdict's destination is reached, and the sweep is what reaches it (DRE-3385). It promotes a FLEET card to Todo once the dependency gate clears, the WIP cap has room and — for a child of an epic — the second critic has passed the plan since it was approved (DRE-3059). The sweep promotes a WORKBENCH or OPERATOR card to Todo on the same gates too, stamping the marks its verdict declares — `hand-built`, plus `no-code` for OPERATOR — before the move, so the card never sits in Todo unmarked; nothing is dispatched for it, it takes no slot under the WIP cap, and the receipt says whose turn it is. A PARKED card does not leave, and is never reported as stalled; a NEEDS WORK card goes back to Planning, which is the planner's move and not the sweep's. A card carrying no verdict at all is not promoted, whether or not it has a parent epic: the epic's approval says the PLAN was approved, never who builds this piece of it. A verdict approves ONE trip through Planning (DRE-4962): a card that has entered Intake, Green Light, Triage, Canceled, Duplicate or Done since its newest verdict is not promoted — the sweep refuses it `stale-verdict`, says once on the card when the verdict was written, which of those lanes it passed through since and that it needs Planning again to be built, and leaves it here. A later exit from Planning, or for a child its epic's green light, is a fresh approval, because the planning exit does not re-stamp a verdict the card already carries. The check reads the card's lane history, so it is the last gate, asked only of a card every other gate has passed; a history Linear cannot return holds the card that sweep and says nothing on it.
exit.pending: the sweep carries every Todo-bound verdict out of this lane and refuses the rest (DRE-2724, DRE-3385); asserting the transitions needs the history Phase 5 records

writers.text: The planner and mid-epic discovery create here; the sweep and the dead-run cap park here; and the build run parks the card it could not build — a stated blocker, or a run that kept dying past the cap (DRE-2859). A person also lands a card here by sending it back from Green Light — the rejected answer that lane's exit names — or by moving it here by hand; that move approves nothing, and the `stale-verdict` refusal above is what keeps the sweep from building it (DRE-4962).

evidence.text: A routing verdict comment; and, for a child of an epic, an epic that has passed Planning exit.
evidence.pending: the marker exists and the sweep reads it (DRE-2724); asserting that every Backlog card carries one needs the writer at planning exit (DRE-2721)

lanes.name: Todo
lanes.stale_why: a Todo card with no dispatched run is a card nothing is coming for

entrance.text: Its verdict names who builds it here: FLEET for a dispatched agent run, WORKBENCH or OPERATOR for a person — marked `hand-built`, which is what already stops the sweep dispatching a competing run or reporting the card as stranded.
entrance.pending: the sweep promotes a FLEET card and a marked hand-built one (DRE-2724, DRE-3385); asserting occupancy needs the transition history Phase 5 records

exit.text: A dispatched run posts its start receipt and the card moves to In Progress — or, on a hand-built card, the person working it opens the pull request.
exit.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

writers.text: ONE promoter, and it is the sweep: reconcile.py's promote_ready() is the only thing that moves an epic's child into this lane, whether the 15-minute cron reaches it or plan.yml's activate route runs it the moment the second critic passes — the route triggers that promoter, it never promotes itself. It releases a child only once the epic carries a `plan-critic: stage=post result=PASS` marker for the current planning attempt (DRE-3059). It is also the writer that stamps a promoted card's marks — `hand-built`, and `no-code` on an OPERATOR card — and it applies them BEFORE the move, because an unmarked card in this lane is one the nudge loop dispatches an agent at fifteen minutes later (DRE-3385). The build run takes cards out of it.

evidence.text: A verdict whose destination is this lane, no unmet blocking relation, and — for a FLEET card — room under the WIP cap. A hand-built card needs no room: nothing is dispatched for it, so it takes no slot and never counts against the cap while it sits here (DRE-3385).
evidence.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

lanes.stale_why: silent agent deaths requeue from here; 60 minutes is one build's honest ceiling

entrance.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

lanes.name: In Review
lanes.stale_why: the folded lane keeps the longer of the two windows the pair had (120 and 60) — a shorter one re-dispatches reviews that are simply still running
lanes.note: Folded from the two review lanes DRE-2726 retired (DRE-2818 deleted their entries once Linear archived the states). Both meant 'a pull request is open and being checked'; the sweep now keys off the evidence — a verdict bound to the head — rather than off which of two lanes the card sat in.

entrance.text: A pull request is open on the card's branch and is being checked: by the critic, by the verifier, or by the merge gate. The card may arrive here from ANY pre-review lane — Intake, Triage, Planning, Backlog, Todo or In Progress — and not only from In Progress: a pull request opened outside the relay's dispatch has no agent-task run behind it to have written In Progress, so qa-review.yml advances the card itself when the pull request opens (DRE-4179). Green Light is not a pre-review lane for this route: it is the CEO's own queue and a branch existing does not take a card out of it.
entrance.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

exit.text: GitHub merges the pull request and linear-sync writes Done — or the pull request is gone and the card is requeued under the dead-run cap.
exit.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

writers.text: The build run puts cards here; the critic, the gate, the fix run and the sweep move them on. The sweep also FILES a card straight into this lane for every dependabot pull request (DRE-3665): the pull request already exists and is already being checked, so there is nothing to plan or dispatch.

evidence.text: An open pull request; and, once the critic has run, a verdict bound to the head sha.

lanes.off_flow_reason: the guard's own destination for a card returned three times — policing it would bounce the sink straight back to Intake and loop

exit.text: Somebody fixes the card, and it re-enters at Intake. Triage is not a decision queue — a card waiting on the CEO belongs in Green Light.

writers.text: Whatever found the defect: the relay, the sweep, either agent run, or a human.

lanes.name: Canceled
lanes.off_flow_reason: terminal and off the path; the card makes no claim to justify

entrance.text: A human decided the work will not be done — or, for a dependabot card, the pull request it was filed for closed unmerged (DRE-3665) — or, for a card the CEO agreed to cancel on a groomer proposal, the groomer's drain moved it with his reason written onto the card (DRE-4677). In all three a human decided; what differs is who wrote it down.

writers.text: A human — and two mechanisms, each for exactly one class, neither of them deciding anything. The sweep, for a card it filed for a dependabot pull request that then closed without merging (DRE-3665): dependabot superseding its own pull request, or a person closing it, is the decision; the sweep records it. The groomer's drain, for a card the CEO agreed to cancel on a groomer proposal (DRE-4677): the groomer proposes cancellations and the CEO agrees card by card in the console, and his per-card agree is the decision — the drain writes Canceled for exactly the cards on the approved proposal's Cancel table that he did not exclude, with the reason he read written onto each one as a comment. The principle the clause states is unchanged in both: a human decided. What changes is who writes it down.

evidence.text: A human's decision, on the card.
